Hi Sana  thanks for the heads up and for the screenshot.

Short answer: you're right  we've seen a small number of EU customers where Calendly/Chili Piper display the slot in the organizer's timezone rather than normalizing to the browser locale when the DST change falls between booking and meeting date (happened for us on March 29). That causes the invite to flip by one hour for some recipients.

Workarounds we use:
- I'll send an explicit calendar invite with the meeting time specified in CET (Europe/Paris) and include the UTC time in the body. That prevents calendar clients from guessing.
- If you still want to use Calendly, use the "Show times in my time zone" toggle at the top-right of the Calendly page before selecting a slot (some browsers hide this toggle).
- As a fallback we can propose 2-3 fixed slots and I'll create the invite myself.

I'm attaching our short demo deck and proposing these slots in CET:
- Tue Mar 30, 11:00-11:30 CET
- Tue Mar 30, 15:00-15:30 CET
- Wed Mar 31, 09:00-09:30 CET

Which of these works? If none, tell me your preferred window and we'll lock it in manually.

Thanks 
